claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, let me check the official eligibility rules so I can give you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I can help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To start, let me ask you: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex. He's 18 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 18, I need to understand his current situation to determine eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is still in college doing his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in approved education, there are a few more things I need to confirm.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great, thank you. Now I need to ask: **Are you currently responsible for Alex? That is, does he live with you, or are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or the equivalent in kind) towards his upkeep - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me at home, so I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to ensure I have all the information:

**Is Alex in hospital, care, or residential accommodation, or has he started paid work for 24 hours or more a week, or is he claiming certain benefits in his own right such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in hospital or care, and he doesn't work 24 hours a week or anything like that. As for benefits... I'm not actually sure if he receives any benefits in his own right like Universal Credit or ESA. I don't think so, but I'm not certain about that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Let me assess your eligibility based on what you've told me.

Based on the information provided:
- You have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old
- Alex is in approved education (doing A-levels at college)
- You live in the UK (Manchester)
- Alex lives with you at home
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is not in hospital, care, or working 24+ hours per week
- You're uncertain whether Alex is claiming benefits like Universal Credit or ESA in his own right

The key issue here is that one of the disqualifying factors for Child Benefit is if your child "starts getting certain benefits, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit" in their own right. Since you don't have certain information about whether Alex is receiving such benefits, I cannot make a definitive determination of eligibility.

If Alex is **not** claiming Universal Credit, ESA, or similar benefits in his own right, then you would be **eligible** for Child Benefit. However, if he is claiming such benefits, you would be **ineligible**.

I would recommend checking whether Alex has any benefit claims in his own name before applying, as this is a critical factor in determining your eligibility.
